'''Anders Wiman''' (11 February 1865 – 13 August 1959) was a [[Sweden|Swedish]] [[mathematician]]. He is known for his work in [[algebraic geometry]] and [[applications of group theory]].

==Life==
Wiman was born to well-off land-owing farmer family in Hammarlöv, Sweden in 1865. He attended school in Lund, and graduated from secondary school in 1885. In the autumn of the same year, Wiman went to Lund University studying Mathematics, Botany and Latin. He attained Bachelor's degree in 1887 and his Licentiate in 1891.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=O'Connor |first=John J |last2=Robertson |first2=Edmund F |title=Anders Wiman |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Wiman/ |website=MacTutor History of Mathematics archive. School of Mathematics and Statistics, University of St Andrews, Scotland.}}</ref> He continued his study in the same university under supervision of [[Carl Fabian Björling]] and was awarded [[doctorate]] in 1892, with thesis ''Klassifikation af regelytorna af sjette graden'' (Classification of regular surfaces of degree 6).

In 1892, Wiman was appointed as a docent (equivalent of assistant professor) in Lund University. There, his work on the classification of finite geometrical groups in the last few years of the 19th century was seen impressive. He classified all algebraic curves of genus 3, 4, 5 and 6 which have non-trivial algebraic automorphisms. In a paper for approximations to small denominators in 1900, Wiman applied measure theory to the probabilistic problem, and became the first person to do so.

In 1901, Wiman accepted an extraordinary professorship in algebra and number theory at [[Uppsala University]]. Topics he studied here included solubility of algebraic equations, [[Galois group]] of soluble equations of prime degree, and [[entire function]]s. Wiman was promoted to an ordinary professor in 1906, and held the chair at Uppsala until 1929. In that year, Wiman was made professor emeritus, but he remained active in teaching.<ref name=":0" />

In 1904 Wiman was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in Heidelberg.<ref>{{cite book |title=Verhandlungen des dritten Mathematiker-Kongresses in Heidelberg von 8. bis 13. August 1904 |publisher=B. G. Teubner |year=1905 |location=Leipzig |pages=190–193 |chapter=''Die metazyklischen Gleichungen 9. Grades'' von A. Wiman |chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=miun.aag4063.0004.001;view=1up;seq=206}}</ref> Wiman was from 1908 an editor of [[Acta Mathematica]].

Wiman returned to Lund in his final year, and stayed there until he died.<ref name=":0" />

==Awards and honours==
He was a member of the:

* [[Royal Physiographic Society in Lund]] (1900)
* [[Royal Society of Sciences in Uppsala]] (1905)
* [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] (1905)
* [[Royal Society of Arts and Sciences in Gothenburg]] (1920);

He was also an honorary member of the Royal Society of Sciences in Uppsala (1938).<ref name=":0" />

==Work==
The main focus of Wiman's research was algebraic geometry and applications of group theory to geometry and function theory. He proved that  for ''n'' > 7, in less than ''n''–2 dimensions, there are no groups of collineations that are isomorphic to the [[symmetric group|symmetric]] or [[alternating group]] on ''n'' symbols. He also determined all finite groups of birational transformations of the plane.<ref>Anders Wiman: ''[http://www.digizeitschriften.de/dms/resolveppn/?PPN=GDZPPN002256118 Zur Theorie der endlichen Gruppen von birationalen Transformationen in der Ebene]'' (April 1896), [[Mathematische Annalen]] 48, September 1896, pp. 195–240</ref> Wiman wrote the article on finite groups of linear transformations for [[Klein's encyclopedia]].

In function theory he did important work on entire functions. From 1914 to 1916 he introduced what is now called [[Wiman-Valiron theory]] (named after him and [[Georges Valiron]]).<ref name=":0" /><ref>Anders Wiman: ''Über den Zusammenhang zwischen dem Maximalbetrage einer analytischen Funktion und dem grössten Gliede der zugehörigen Taylor’schen Reihe'', Acta Mathematica 37, December 1914, pp. 305–326</ref><ref>Anders Wiman: ''Über den Zusammenhang zwischen dem Maximalbetrage einer analytischen Funktion und dem grössten Beitrage bei gegebenem Argumente der Funktion'', Acta Mathematica 41, December 1916, pp. 1–28</ref><ref>Hayman, W. K. (1974). [https://books.google.com/books?id=eCvriuu28BgC&pg=PA317 The local growth of power series: a survey of the Wiman-Valiron method.] [[Canadian Mathematical Bulletin]], 17(3), 317–358.</ref> Wiman's generalization of a theorem of Hadamard is known as Wiman's theorem.<ref>Anders Wiman: ''Sur une extension d’un théorème de M. Hadamard'' (7. Juni 1905), Arkiv för Matematik, Astronomi och Fysik, vol. 2, issue 14, 1905, pp. 1–5 {{in lang|fr}}</ref><ref>Anders Wiman: ''[http://www.digizeitschriften.de/dms/resolveppn/?PPN=GDZPPN00226594X Über eine Eigenschaft der ganzen Funktionen von der Höhe Null]'' (11 February 1914), [[Mathematische Annalen]] 76, March 1915, pp. 197–211</ref> Wiman's theorems for quasiregular mappings shows that an entire holomorphic function of order less than 1/2 has a minimum modulus converging to along a sequence.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Martio |first=O. |last2=Miklyukov |first2=V. M. |last3=Vuorinen |first3=M. |date=December 2010 |title=Wiman and Arima Theorems for Quasiregular Mappings |url=https://journalofinequalitiesandapplications.springeropen.com/articles/10.1155/2010/604217 |journal=Journal of Inequalities and Applications |language=en |volume=2010 |issue=1 |pages=1–29 |doi=10.1155/2010/604217 |issn=1029-242X|doi-access=free |arxiv=1002.2500 }}</ref>

He also introduced [[Wiman's sextic curve]], the Wiman inequality, and the Wiman bound.<ref name=":0" />

His investigations on the zeros of the derivatives of entire functions — along with similar investigations by [[George Pólya]] – had a great influence on the theory of entire functions; in particular, the now-proved Wiman conjecture,<ref>Terence Sheil-Small: ''On the zeros of the derivatives of real entire functions and Wiman’s conjecture'', Annals of Mathematics (2) 129, 1989, pp. 179–193 {{doi|10.2307/1971490}}</ref>
<ref>W. Bergweiler, A. Eremenko and J. Langley: ''Real entire functions of infinite order and a conjecture of Wiman, [[Geometric and Functional Analysis]] (GAFA), 13, 5 (2003), 975-991.''</ref> and the now-proved Pólya-Wiman conjecture<ref>Thomas Craven, George Csordas, Wayne Smith: ''The zeros of derivatives of entire functions and the Pólya-Wiman conjecture'', Annals of Mathematics (2) 125, 1987, pp. 405–431 {{doi|10.2307/1971315}}</ref> have inspired much research.

==Notable PhD students==
[[Arne Beurling]] (1933) and [[Fritz Carlson]] (1914) were among his students in Uppsala University.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anders Wiman - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=19965 |access-date=2022-06-29 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref>
